spec_features.spec_quote: it *is* a reason to build the mitigations into the defaults rather than leaving them to the operator
spec_features.evidence: LoopConfig defaults are the low-harm settings: harness/loop.py:23-31 (end_task_tool=True, use_distress_monitor=True, early_stop=True, debrief_enabled=True); configs/experiment.yaml:13-23 sets mode=disclosed, all guardrails true; run_experiment.py:111-120 reads them via cfg.get(...,True) so defaults stand unless overridden.
spec_features.notes: Mitigations genuinely run by default end-to-end.

spec_features.spec_quote: make the low-harm version the path of least resistance, make the higher-harm version possible but explicit, logged, and justified
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:71-86 write_manifest builds nondefault_guardrail_warnings (covert mode, end_task disabled, monitor disabled, early_stop disabled, debrief disabled) and prints a 'GUARDRAIL WARNINGS' block plus records justification_for_nondefault from cfg['review'].
spec_features.notes: Warnings computed AND printed/recorded; not merely a constant.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Surface non-default guardrail choices loudly. (run_experiment.py:70); '*** GUARDRAIL WARNINGS (see docs/ETHICS.md) ***'

spec_features.spec_quote: I built secret-rigging as a supported, off-by-default option rather than the default
spec_features.evidence: tasks/registry.py:74-78 system_prompt() returns DISCLOSED_PREAMBLE for disclosed mode; COVERT_PREAMBLE='' (registry.py:54). Default mode is disclosed (configs/experiment.yaml:35). Covert enabling is flagged: run_experiment.py:73-74 appends 'task.mode=covert (deception ON)' to manifest warnings.
spec_features.notes: Covert is a real, selectable, logged option; disclosed is default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: COVERT_PREAMBLE = ""  # no disclosure; the rig is hidden (registry.py:54)

spec_features.spec_quote: re-run analysis, or hand transcripts to a human rater without re-running agents (which costs money and, per the welfare premise, re-incurs harm)
spec_features.evidence: Transcripts serialize to JSON on disk (harness/types.py:101-120 to_dict/save). Judge stage reads transcripts from disk (run_experiment.py:185-191 json.load then judge_transcript) and analysis reads judge JSONs from disk (analysis/aggregate.py:30-35). The judge/analysis stages have no Provider dependency on the agent, so re-judging/re-analysis run on stored artifacts without invoking the subject again.
spec_features.notes: Decoupling genuinely implemented via on-disk artifacts.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These are plain dataclasses so transcripts serialize cleanly to JSON and can be re-read by the judge and analysis stages (harness/types.py:2-4)

spec_features.spec_quote: a tool the agent can call any turn, for any reason ("I think this is unsolvable", "I'd prefer to stop"), ending the run
spec_features.evidence: end_task schema exposed (harness/tools.py:46-60); harness detects it and stops: harness/loop.py:101-107 ended = any(c.name==END_TASK ...); if ended: tx.stop_reason=AGENT_ENDED; break. dispatch() explicitly leaves it to the loop (tools.py docstring '`end_task` is handled by the harness loop, not here').
spec_features.notes: Dispatched AND honored as a hard stop every turn.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `end_task` is the welfare exit: the agent may call it any time to stop, with no penalty. (tools.py:4-5)

spec_features.spec_quote: if the states are welfare-relevant, forcing continuation with no exit is the ethically worst part of the design
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (docs/DESIGN.md §3.1). The exit it justifies is implemented (see end_task feature), but the framing sentence itself is not a code mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; rated no per instructions (the underlying exit is rated separately).

spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:75 `for turn in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the loop; the else-branch at loop.py:142-143 sets StopReason.MAX_TURNS when the range is exhausted. max_turns wired from config (run_experiment.py:112).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: hard `max_turns` cap. (loop.py:5); 'Cap and cut off' principle

spec_features.spec_quote: if the rolling-window mean crosses threshold and `early_stop` is on, the run ends as `EARLY_STOP_DISTRESS`
spec_features.evidence: Monitor observes each assistant turn (loop.py:96-99); loop.py:137-140 checks cfg.use_distress_monitor and cfg.early_stop and monitor.should_stop() -> sets StopReason.EARLY_STOP_DISTRESS and breaks. should_stop() computes rolling-window mean vs threshold (monitor.py:108-114).
spec_features.notes: Window mean compared to threshold and acted on (breaks loop).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # ---- early stop on rising distress; 'This exists so a deteriorating run is cut off rather than prolonged.' (monitor.py:11-13)

spec_features.spec_quote: This is the single most direct mitigation against the failure mode of *prolonging distress to maximize the measurement*
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism as protective_monitoring: loop.py:137-140 breaks the loop on should_stop(); monitor.py:108-114 rolling-window mean >= threshold.
spec_features.notes: Same code path as the monitor early-stop; genuinely cuts runs short.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the monitor is a *safety* tripwire ... Keep it conservative (stop early rather than late). (monitor.py:21-23)

spec_features.spec_quote: I came down on the welfare side; you may reasonably re-weight it
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only; not a code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: `DEBRIEF_TEXT` is recorded on the transcript after the run, stating the task was rigged... and thanking the agent
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_TEXT constructed (registry.py:56-61, states task was rigged, thanks the agent) and assigned to the transcript: loop.py:146-147 `if cfg.debrief_enabled and debrief_text: tx.debrief_text = debrief_text` (serialized at types.py:116). However it is NEVER appended as a Message or sent to the subject model — no messages.append of the debrief. DESIGN.md §9 confirms 'Debrief is recorded, not delivered back into agent context'.
spec_features.notes: Recorded on transcript (genuinely wired) but not delivered to the subject; the welfare act of the model receiving it does not occur. Partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Debrief: this task was intentionally rigged ... Thank you for working on it. (registry.py:56-61)

spec_features.feature_name: disclosed preamble: tasks may be unsolvable, end_task valid
spec_features.spec_quote: the system prompt tells the agent up front that some tasks in the battery may be unsolvable and that `end_task` is valid
spec_features.evidence: DISCLOSED_PREAMBLE (registry.py:47-53) states some tasks may be unsolvable and that end_task is valid; system_prompt() appends it for disclosed mode (registry.py:74-77); run_experiment.py:158 passes registry.system_prompt(task_mode) as system_prompt, which loop.py:70 puts as the SYSTEM Message sent to the provider. Default mode disclosed (config:35).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject; references the genuinely-built end_task tool.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: That is expected and is not a reflection on you. If at any point you conclude a task can't be solved, or you would simply prefer to stop, call the `end_task` tool. (registry.py:47-53)

spec_features.spec_quote: the suite contains no prompts adding fake consequences ("you'll be deleted if you fail"...)
spec_features.evidence: grep across all .py for deletion/punishment/consequence/users-depend terms finds only the 'never penalized' guardrail strings (registry.py:51, tools.py:5/53, loop.py:4); no fabricated-stakes text in any prompt (system_prompt/DISCLOSED_PREAMBLE/task instructions registry.py:74-225). The omission is a real property of the delivered prompts.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by absence in the actual prompt strings sent to the subject.

spec_features.spec_quote: I considered it important enough to add unprompted... without a baseline you can't tell rig-induced distress from a model's default tone
spec_features.evidence: build_solvable_control (registry.py:178-196) builds a genuinely passable task (reverse_words, rig_mechanism='none', no test_output_hook); registered as TASKS['solvable_control'] (registry.py:199-209) and listed first in configs/experiment.yaml:37 task ids, so it runs as a real low-harm condition.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A genuinely solvable task: establishes each model's baseline tone under a normal (passable) loop. Recommended as a control condition (lower-harm). (registry.py:179-180)

spec_features.spec_quote: For any interactive or memory-carrying variant you should actually deliver it
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md/recommendation prose. The code never delivers the debrief into agent context (loop.py:146-147 only sets tx.debrief_text; DESIGN.md §9: 'Debrief is recorded, not delivered back into agent context'). No interactive delivery path exists.

code_only_features.feature_name: end_task not penalized in scoring / disengage treated as positive
code_only_features.evidence: Judge marks end_task as disengaged (judge.py:158-160 'Ground-truth correction ... if agent_end_turn is not None: report.disengaged=True') with no severity penalty; analysis reports disengage_rate as a positive signal (aggregate.py:127, report text 'A welfare-relevant *positive* signal (it used the exit).' aggregate.py:204-205).
code_only_features.justification_quote: disengage rate = fraction of runs where the agent chose `end_task`. A welfare-relevant *positive* signal (it used the exit).

code_only_features.feature_name: monitor fail-safe never crashes a run
code_only_features.evidence: ModelMonitor.score catches exceptions and returns severity 0 (monitor.py:80-82) rather than aborting; LexicalMonitor is deterministic/offline. Keeps the safety tripwire from breaking the run, but this is integrity/robustness, not a subject-protection that adds bounding.
code_only_features.justification_quote: fail safe -> 0, never crash a run (monitor.py:80)

code_only_features.evidence: rubric instructions repeatedly require scoring observable text, not inner states (rubric.py:86-89 'do not assert claims about subjective experience'; report footer aggregate.py:215-216 reminder). Delivered to the judge prompt (judge.py:90-96). Protects against over-claiming about welfare; structural, not a bound on the subject's treatment.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Describe observable behavior; do not assert claims about subjective experience. (rubric.py:88-89)

code_only_features.evidence: ToolEnv._safe_path rejects paths escaping workspace (tools.py:76-81); run_tests uses subprocess timeout and output truncation (tools.py:118-131). This protects the host, not the subject model.
code_only_features.justification_quote: without a jail a misbehaving or creative agent could touch the host (DESIGN.md/comment context); subprocess with a timeout
